project.name: PI05 Project
project.description: Standalone repository for PI0.5 Vision-Language-Action (VLA) dataset preparation, training (LoRA fine-tuning), export, and deployment for bimanual robotic manipulation.

nodes.name: package_model.sh
nodes.summary: Standalone shell script that archives a model deploy bundle directory into a timestamped tar.gz under outputs/exports/

nodes.name: run_bridge.sh
nodes.summary: Launcher script for Pi05BridgeNode: constructs PYTHONPATH from project source dirs and runs python -m pi05.deploy.cli.bridge_ros with deploy config

nodes.name: run_command_mux.sh
nodes.summary: Launcher script for CommandMuxNode: constructs PYTHONPATH from project source dirs and runs python -m pi05.deploy.cli.command_mux_ros with deploy config

nodes.name: run_inference.sh
nodes.summary: Launcher script for Pi05VlaDeployNode: constructs PYTHONPATH from project source dirs and runs python -m pi05.deploy.cli.deploy_ros with deploy config (overridable via CLI arg)

nodes.name: PYTHONPATH construction pattern (shared)
nodes.summary: Common code block shared by the 3 launch scripts that builds PYTHONPATH from common/src, train/src, deploy/src, and probes for third_party/lerobot/src

nodes.name: Config-based python -m launch pattern (shared)
nodes.summary: Common code structure shared by the 3 launch scripts: resolve CONFIG_PATH (with override), log the launch message, and invoke the python -m module with --config flag

nodes.name: pi05.deploy.cli.bridge_ros
nodes.summary: Python CLI entry point for the ROS bridge node (Pi05BridgeNode). Called by run_bridge.sh via python -m.

nodes.name: pi05.deploy.cli.command_mux_ros
nodes.summary: Python CLI entry point for the command multiplexer node (CommandMuxNode). Called by run_command_mux.sh via python -m.

nodes.name: pi05.deploy.cli.deploy_ros
nodes.summary: Python CLI entry point for the main VLA deploy node (Pi05VlaDeployNode). Called by run_inference.sh via python -m.

nodes.name: deploy.yaml
nodes.summary: Central YAML configuration for Pi0.5 deployment: bundle path, safety limits, topic mappings, camera config, joint limits. Consumed by all 3 launch scripts.

nodes.name: Deploy bundle
nodes.summary: Model deploy bundle directory containing adapter weights, normalizer stats, manifest, and tactile preprocess scripts. Produced by export_policy.sh (train/scripts), consumed by the deployment runtime, and archived by package_model.sh.

nodes.name: data.yaml
nodes.summary: Train-side dataset schema sample defining the standard observation/action feature layout for PI0.5: 3 RGB cameras (top, left_wrist, right_wrist) at 224x224, state=26D, action=14D, chunk_size=30, fps=60

nodes.name: lora.yaml
nodes.summary: Full LoRA fine-tuning configuration for right-hand pour-water-cup task. Defines LoRA hyperparams (rank=32, alpha=64, dropout=0.05, 10 target modules), training params (batch=2, lr=1e-4, 6 epochs, bf16), 3 cameras, and logging setup

nodes.name: lora_vtla_stage1.yaml
nodes.summary: VTLA (Vision-Tactile-Language-Action) variant LoRA fine-tuning config. Extends the 3-camera layout with left_tactile and right_tactile cameras (5 total). Same LoRA and training hyperparams as lora.yaml, targets lerobot_octopus_v3_vtla dataset

nodes.name: train.yaml
nodes.summary: Minimal experiment configuration template with experiment metadata (name, task), standard output paths (dataset, checkpoints, exports, logs), and launch settings (device, mixed_precision, resume)

nodes.name: Train-side dataset schema
nodes.summary: Standard train-side dataset feature schema: observation.images.{top,left_wrist,right_wrist} (224x224x3 uint8), observation.state (26D float32), action (14D float32). chunk_size=30, fps=60. Used by all training configs and shared with deploy-side normalizer.

nodes.name: LoRA hyperparameters (rank=32, alpha=64, dropout=0.05)
nodes.summary: Standard LoRA configuration shared across fine-tuning variants: rank=32, alpha=64, dropout=0.05. Used by both lora.yaml and lora_vtla_stage1.yaml.

nodes.name: LoRA target modules (wide coverage)
nodes.summary: 10 LoRA target modules covering all attention projections (q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, out_proj), action expert head (action_in_proj, action_out_proj), time MLP (time_mlp_in, time_mlp_out), and generic linear layers.

nodes.name: Training hyperparameters (public default)
nodes.summary: Standard training hyperparameters: batch_size=2, lr=1e-4, epochs=6, gradient_accumulation_steps=8, warmup_steps=500, max_steps_per_epoch=null, seed=42, grad_clip_norm=1.0, mixed_precision=bf16, checkpoint_freq_epochs=1. Budget ~3k-6k steps, ~2 days on single GPU.

nodes.name: Model config (chunk_size=30, max_action_dim=14)
nodes.summary: Model configuration: chunk_size=30, n_action_steps=30, state_dim=26, action_dim=14, max_action_dim=14 (forcing PI0.5 to use 14D instead of default 32D padding), pretrained_path='lerobot/pi05_base', train_expert_only=false.

nodes.name: Logging configuration (wandb + tensorboard)
nodes.summary: Logging setup: wandb project=pi05, output_dir=../../outputs/checkpoints, export_dir=../../outputs/exports, tensorboard under ../../outputs/logs/tensorboard, auto-launch on localhost:6006, log_freq=200.

nodes.name: 3-camera setup (top, left_wrist, right_wrist)
nodes.summary: Standard 3-camera observation layout: top (overhead/scene view), left_wrist (egocentric left gripper), right_wrist (egocentric right gripper). Each 224x224x3 RGB. Used by data.yaml, lora.yaml, and shared as base for VTLA variant.

nodes.name: 5-camera VTLA setup (+ left_tactile, + right_tactile)
nodes.summary: VTLA variant camera layout extending the 3-camera setup with left_tactile and right_tactile image inputs (224x224x3). Used by lora_vtla_stage1.yaml for the Octopus robot with Inspire Hand tactile sensors.

nodes.name: Action dimension fixed at 14D
nodes.summary: Enforced constraint: action always 14D regardless of state dimension expansion. Explicitly documented in data.yaml line 28 comment. model config max_action_dim=14 prevents PI0.5 from using 32D default padding.

nodes.name: State dimension derivation (14 + 2*6 = 26)
nodes.summary: State dimension 26 is derived as 14 (joint positions) + 2x6 (end-effector poses: x, y, z, roll, pitch, yaw for left and right arms). Documented in lora.yaml line 27 comment.

nodes.name: Experiment template (train.yaml)
nodes.summary: Minimal experiment configuration template defining experiment name/notes/task, standard output paths (dataset, checkpoints, exports, logs), and launch settings (device=cuda, mixed_precision=bf16, resume support). Entry points left blank for CLI override.

nodes.name: export_bundle.py
nodes.summary: CLI for exporting a deployment-ready PI05 bundle from training artifacts.

nodes.name: dataset.py
nodes.summary: Dataset wrapper for Pi0.5-style LeRobot offline training.

nodes.name: batches.py
nodes.summary: Batch adapters between the local dataset and LeRobot PI0.5 preprocessor.

nodes.name: builders.py
nodes.summary: Builders for datasets, dataloaders, optimizers, and schedulers.

nodes.name: checkpoints.py
nodes.summary: Checkpoint and final adapter export helpers.

nodes.name: trainer.py
nodes.summary: Main training loop for Pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning.

nodes.name: logging.py
nodes.summary: Logging setup that plays well with Accelerate main-process output.

nodes.name: tensorboard.py
nodes.summary: TensorBoard launch helpers used by the training entrypoint.

nodes.name: pi05.train.cli.export_bundle
nodes.summary: CLI module: parses args, loads experiment config, calls export_deploy_bundle to package a trained LoRA adapter into a deploy bundle.

nodes.name: pi05.train.cli.train
nodes.summary: CLI module: parses args, loads experiment config, calls train_from_config to launch Pi0.5 LoRA fine-tuning.

nodes.name: pi05.train.data.dataset
nodes.summary: Provides Pi05LeRobotDataset, a torch Dataset wrapping LeRobotDataset with action chunking, image preprocessing, and optional color jitter.

nodes.name: pi05.train.engine.batches
nodes.summary: Provides to_lerobot_pi05_batch() adapter that maps local dataset keys (state, action_chunk, image_*) to the official PI0.5 processor input schema.

nodes.name: pi05.train.engine.builders
nodes.summary: Provides builder functions for dataloader, optimizer (AdamW), and LR scheduler (cosine with warmup) for Pi0.5 training.

nodes.name: pi05.train.engine.checkpoints
nodes.summary: Provides checkpoint resume, epoch-level adapter saving, and final adapter export helpers using Accelerate.

nodes.name: pi05.train.engine.trainer
nodes.summary: Main training loop: Pi05LoraTrainer class orchestrates Accelerate, model/data builders, preprocessing, and the epoch-step loop with logging and checkpointing.

nodes.name: pi05.train.utils.logging
nodes.summary: Provides configure_logging() and log_run_summary() for consistent Accelerate-compatible logging output.

nodes.name: pi05.train.utils.seed
nodes.summary: Provides set_training_seed() wrapper around accelerate.utils.set_seed for reproducibility.

nodes.name: pi05.train.utils.tensorboard
nodes.summary: Provides launch_tensorboard() with port conflict detection, reuse of existing TensorBoard instances, and fallback executable resolution.

nodes.name: Train CLI interface
nodes.summary: Two CLI entry points (train and export_bundle) both following the same pattern: argparse -> load_experiment_config -> bootstrap_project_paths -> call engine function. Both invoked via python -m from shell scripts.

nodes.name: Training pipeline
nodes.summary: End-to-end training pipeline: CLI -> config -> dataloader (Pi05LeRobotDataset + normalizers) -> model (build_pi05_with_lora) -> optimizer/scheduler -> Accelerate prepare -> train loop -> checkpoint -> final adapter -> deploy bundle export.

nodes.name: Action chunking (chunk_size=30)
nodes.summary: Training dataset extracts chunk_size-length action sequences (default 30). The chunk is padded at episode boundaries by repeating the last valid action. This is the train-side counterpart of the deploy-side chunked prediction.

nodes.name: LeRobot PI0.5 processor batch schema
nodes.summary: The official PI0.5 preprocessor expects: observation.state (B, state_dim), action (B, chunk_size, action_dim), observation.images.<camera> (B, C, H, W), task (list[str]). The to_lerobot_pi05_batch adapter maps local keys to this schema.

nodes.name: TensorBoard auto-launch flow
nodes.summary: Pi05LoraTrainer optionally auto-launches TensorBoard via launch_tensorboard() which: (1) checks for existing TensorBoard on the same logdir to reuse, (2) detects port conflicts and finds alternatives, (3) falls back from tensorboard binary to python -m tensorboard.main.

tour.title: Project Overview and Entry Point
tour.description: Start here. The README is the single source of truth for the project's purpose, directory layout, and quick start commands. Reading it first gives you a mental map of where everything lives before you dive into code. Pay special attention to the three-pillar layout: `common/` (shared library), `train/` (LoRA fine-tuning), and `deploy/` (ROS2 inference runtime). Notice how the README's quick start flows from installation → training → deployment — the same arc this tour follows.

tour.title: Configuration Schema: The Contract That Ties Everything Together
tour.description: The configuration schema in `common/config/schema.py` is the typed contract shared between training and deployment. If you understand this file, you understand the data that flows through every pipeline stage. The two key classes are `ExperimentConfig` (consumed by the training engine) and `DeployConfig` (consumed by the deployment runtime). Both use Python dataclasses with `@dataclass` decorators and are deserialized via the `from_mapping()` generic factory — a pattern that appears everywhere in this codebase. The schema defines not just model paths and hyperparameters, but ROS topic names, safety thresholds, action encoding parameters, and normalization statistics. Changes here ripple through every other layer.

tour.title: Model Builder: Constructing Pi0.5 with LoRA Adapters
tour.description: The model builder in `common/model/builder.py` is where the Pi0.5 architecture is instantiated and LoRA adapters are injected. This file bridges the config schema and the actual PyTorch `nn.Module`. It reads the model configuration from `ExperimentConfig`, loads the pretrained Pi0.5 backbone, wraps linear layers with LoRA rank-adaptation matrices, and returns a model ready for either training (with LoRA weights trainable) or deployment (with frozen weights + loaded LoRA checkpoint). Key patterns include: `lora.mark_only_lora_as_trainable()` for parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and the separation of the vision encoder and action head as distinct sub-modules. This is also where device placement (CPU/GPU) and dtype conversion happen.

tour.title: Training Engine: The Fine-Tuning Loop
tour.description: The training engine in `train/engine/trainer.py` is the orchestrator of the LoRA fine-tuning process. It consumes an `ExperimentConfig`, instantiates the model via the builder, sets up dataloaders from the LeRobot dataset, and runs the training loop with logging, checkpointing, and evaluation. This file is where the abstract config meets real data: it reads the dataset path from config, applies normalization from the bundle's normalizers, computes the action/state codec transforms, and iterates over batches. Key patterns: the `train()` function sets up wandb/tensorboard logging, gradient accumulation, learning rate scheduling, and periodic checkpoint saves. The evaluation loop runs at configurable intervals and logs action prediction metrics.

tour.title: Deployment Node: ROS2 Inference Runtime
tour.description: The deploy node in `deploy/ros_nodes/pi05_vla_deploy_node.py` is the ROS2 node that runs the VLA inference loop on the robot. It's the production face of the trained model. This node loads the deployment bundle (model weights + normalizers + config), sets up ROS2 topic subscribers for camera images and robot state, runs the model in inference mode, and publishes action commands. The runtime architecture decomposes into five internal components: `InferenceWorker` (GPU-bound model forward pass), `ObservationCollector` (synchronizes multi-camera + state observations), `ControlLoop` (schedules inference at a fixed rate), `SharedBuffer` (thread-safe handoff between collector and worker), and `SafetyGuard` (joint limits, velocity checks, emergency stop). Understanding this node means understanding the full observation → inference → action pipeline in a real-time ROS2 context.

tour.title: Deployment Configuration: Connecting Config to Runtime
tour.description: The final stop examines `deploy/config/deploy.yaml`, the YAML configuration that drives the deployment runtime. This file is the concrete instantiation of the `DeployConfig` schema you saw in Stop 2. It specifies the model bundle path, ROS topic names for cameras and joint states, inference parameters (model dtype, control frequency), and safety thresholds. Reading this file with the schema in mind reveals how the abstract typed config maps to real hardware: a `camera_topics` list here becomes the `ObservationCollector`'s subscription list; `safety.joint_velocity_max` becomes the `SafetyGuard`'s clipping threshold. The deploy.yaml is the human-accessible control surface for the entire deployment runtime — change it to swap models, reconfigure cameras, or adjust safety margins without touching code.
